document.title: Reagan Letter to Gandhi
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), A New Phase in the Great Game: U.S., Soviets, India, Pakistan vied to shape a new Afghanistan in late 1980s | National Security Archive
document.note: Reagan responds to Gandhi's December 4 letter, reflecting on Afghanistan talks with Gorbachev at the summit. He says Gorbachev is wedded to Najibullah's coalition approach, and notes no movement on Afghanistan despite the INF Treaty.

events.description: Reagan-Gorbachev summit; Reagan pressed for firm Soviet withdrawal timetable from Afghanistan; INF agreement to eliminate a class of nuclear weapons.
Reagan letter to Gandhi on Afghanistan and nuclear issues.
Reagan–Gorbachev summit discussed Afghanistan, with no movement on a withdrawal timetable, and agreed on nuclear arms reductions.
US and India agreed on a program of bilateral cooperation during Gandhi's visit to the US.
Gandhi sent a letter to Reagan about the summit and South Asian nuclear programs.
Reagan sent a letter to Gandhi reporting on the summit and Afghanistan.
Najibullah publicly proposed Soviet troop withdrawal in no more than 12 months.
Reagan planned to go to Moscow the next year for a possible arms-reduction signing.

key_claims: Reagan stressed that an Afghan settlement depended on the Soviet Union setting a firm timetable for troop withdrawal.
Gorbachev reiterated the intention to withdraw but avoided a specific commitment beyond noting Najibullah's 12-month proposal.
Gorbachev linked beginning of withdrawals to the end of outside interference.
The US held that Afghans should decide their political future and viewed Najibullah's coalition as unrealistic.
Reagan asked Gandhi to share concerns with the Soviets on Afghanistan.
Reagan reaffirmed unchanged non-proliferation policy toward India and Pakistan after the Senate committee proposal failed.
